title: Paradigm Shift in Cosmology: Continuous Energy Recycling Through the Grid-Higgs Framework
description: The paper synthesizes the Energy-Flow (EFC) and Grid-Higgs frameworks to propose a cosmology with continuous energy recycling, reinterpreting the CMB as an ongoing process rather than a relic. It replaces dark matter with entropy-driven "entropic tension" between Higgs-anchored spacetime nodes and argues for near-standard behavior except at entropy extremes, offering quantitative, testable deviations in CMB anisotropies and lensing.

entropy_wave_driver.description: Postulated relation for early-universe entropy waves coupling energy flow to entropy S and temperature T, used to set thermal conditions for primordial abundances.

linear_energy_flow.description: Stated linear decline of energy flow from the singular (S=0) to the Altular maximum-entropy state (S=1), with \rho_0 the initial reference density.

key_results.main_finding: Using 10 free parameters (including entropy gradients and Higgs-node density), the model reports χ² ≈ 0 over ℓ = 100–1500 for ACT/WMAP CMB fits and claims natural reproduction of rotation curves and specific, testable deviations in lensing and high-ℓ CMB anisotropies.
parameters_tested: α (entropy-wave coupling in δEf = α S T^4)

sealed_predictions.statement: High-ℓ CMB anisotropies will show systematic 7–10% deviations from ΛCDM for ℓ > 1000 due to continuous CMB recycling at the Altular boundary.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Precise TT/TE/EE spectra from ACT, SPT-3G, and Simons Observatory up to ℓ ≳ 3000.

sealed_predictions.statement: Weak-lensing signals in low-entropy (void-like) environments will deviate by up to 15% from GR+ΛCDM predictions because of entropic-tension effects across Higgs-node gradients.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic weak-lensing and galaxy–galaxy lensing in voids from DES, HSC, KiDS, and LSST Y1–Y10 analyses.

sealed_predictions.statement: Galactic rotation curves can be fit without invoking particle dark matter, using entropic tension from the Grid-Higgs structure.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Meta-analysis of large rotation-curve samples (e.g., SPARC) showing systematic residuals that still require dark halos after applying the EFC entropic-tension prescription.

sealed_predictions.statement: Gravitational-wave propagation matches GR under typical conditions but exhibits measurable deviations only near entropy extremes (S≈0 or S≈1).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint GW–EM constraints on dispersion and speed from LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA events, especially those near SMBH environments or extreme-density regions.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-precision CMB measurements (ACT/SPT/Simons Observatory) show <1–2% agreement with ΛCDM at ℓ > 1000, ruling out the predicted 7–10% deviations.
KC2: Weak-lensing maps in low-entropy/void regions exhibit <5% deviation from GR+ΛCDM, contradicting the model's up-to-15% prediction.
KC3: Comprehensive rotation-curve datasets (e.g., SPARC) continue to require dark halos after implementing the entropic-tension prescription, with statistically significant residuals.
KC4: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis abundances (H/He/Li) cannot be matched within 5% for any choice of α in δEf = α S T^4 under the model's thermal history.
KC5: Multimessenger GW events impose bounds inconsistent with the model by showing no entropy-dependent propagation effects even near putative S-extreme environments.
KC6: High-fidelity CMB isotropy and polarization results demand standard inflationary initial conditions with no evidence for continuous recycling, contradicting the model's mechanism.
